claim: Illustrative Adam state ledger totals 16 bytes per parameter under the stated dtypes and separate master-weight assumption.
conditions: 2-byte weights, 2-byte gradients, 4-byte master copy, two 4-byte moments. This is a chosen accounting model, not a universal framework allocation.

claim: The stages partition optimizer state, then gradients, then parameters.
conditions: Stage definitions; parameter materialization and residency policies require separate accounting.

claim: For 7B parameters across eight balanced shards, the ideal persistent byte totals are 112e9, 38.5e9, 26.25e9, and 14e9.
conditions: The lesson’s fixed Adam policy; no activations, buffers or transient materialization. Unit-tested arithmetic, not measured GPU allocations.

claim: The historical experimental implementation includes a subset of the paper’s proposed optimizations.
conditions: Version 3 §10 and Table 3; do not reinterpret as an isolated full-parameter-sharding experiment.

claim: FSDP2 exposes materialization, resharding and mixed-precision policies.
conditions: Versioned documentation inspected; no implementation executed or performance reproduced.

claim: A later tiny profiling exercise can expose the gap between a persistent floor and a step’s measured peak.
conditions: Proposed bounded experiment only; not performed by Richard or this research.

claim: The peak memory and throughput of an actual future training run cannot be established by the estimator.
conditions: Requires actual model, data shapes, hardware, optimizer and framework schedule; arbitrary allowances are not measurements.

claim: ReduceScatter followed by AllGather is equivalent to AllReduce, and every rank must call a collective with the same count and datatype.
conditions: NCCL 2.32.3 semantics. The page states no further ordering rule; the lesson does not claim one.

claim: A ring allgather costs (p − 1)α + (p − 1)/p · nβ, and its bandwidth term cannot be reduced further.
conditions: α + nβ point-to-point model on a switched cluster; reduction arithmetic and contention excluded.

claim: A ring all-reduce costs about 2(p − 1)α + 2(p − 1)/p · n/B, and latency equals bandwidth at n* = pαB (6.4 MB for 32 ranks, 5 µs, 40 GB/s).
conditions: Ring algorithm only, assumed α and B, no tree or hierarchical algorithms, no reduction cost.

claim: Bus bandwidth scales algorithm bandwidth by 2(n − 1)/n for all-reduce and (n − 1)/n for all-gather and reduce-scatter.
conditions: nccl-tests reporting convention; the all-reduce factor is a best case for point-to-point algorithms.

claim: DistributedDataParallel buckets gradients at 25 MiB by default, and bucket reduction can overlap backward computation.
conditions: PyTorch 2.15.0 documentation; possible overlap, not a measured amount.

claim: Standard data parallelism and ZeRO stages 1–2 move 2Ψ per step; stage 3 moves 3Ψ, 1.5× the baseline.
conditions: ZeRO v3 §7 analysis in parameter counts; ignores the ring's (p − 1)/p factor.

claim: A 7B BF16 model on 8 ranks sends 24.5 GB per rank per step (0.65 s) without stage 3 and 36.75 GB (0.97 s) with it.
conditions: Assumed α = 5 µs, B = 40 GB/s, 25 MiB buckets, ring algorithm; computed by unit-tested functions, not measured.

claim: Megatron tensor parallelism needs two all-reduces per layer in forward and two in backward; a flush pipeline idles (p − 1)/m of ideal time, divided by v when interleaved.
conditions: Megatron-LM v5 §2.2–2.3 and §3.2, for Transformer MLP and self-attention blocks.

claim: PTD-P outperformed ZeRO-3 without model parallelism by 6% and 24% (175B and 530B) at the first GPU counts and by 70% at double the GPUs, attributed to less cross-node communication.
conditions: DGX A100 servers; configurations differ in more than one respect; at 530B ZeRO-3 used 640 GPUs because it did not fit on 560.

claim: For the guide's 70B, 32-GPU scenario, tensor parallelism inside servers with ZeRO-1 across them is the better first pilot than ZeRO-3 across all GPUs.
conditions: Supported by the closest measured comparison and by activation splitting; contradicted by the idealized ring model's near tie. Needs the guide's pilot.

claim: How much of each layout's communication overlaps computation, and how much contention changes the ring model, on a given cluster.
conditions: Requires profiling the intended step on the target network; no public source settles it for another cluster.

claim: Megatron's estimate 8TP/(nX) gives about 83 days for 450B tokens, 1T parameters, 3,072 GPUs at 163 TFLOP/s, consistent with the reported 84.
conditions: Uses the paper's own measured X; excludes failures, restarts and evaluation unless X covers them.
